quest.title: The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent
quest.description: For treasure and for the future of Watatsumi Island, you accept Tsuyuko's commission and prepare to descend into Enkanomiya...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x4, Mora x30000

chapter.title: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku

talks.objective: Go to the ruins up ahead

dialogues.text: Uh-oh! Trying to trespass, are we...?
...Wait, maybe not. I correct myself. You two must be the heroes who have come to retrieve the coral this time, are you not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Two?" Hehe, so you're counting Paimon too?
Haha. Well, I was originally thinking that "Sangonomiya Shrine couldn't possibly be so shorthanded that they're only sending one person, right?"
So consider my expectations exceeded. There's actually two of you.

choices.text: Oh, I know my way around a fight.

response.text: Haha! I love your gusto and optimism! Good stuff!
I hope that by the end of this, you'll count me in the team as well. I'm sure the three of us will get on swimmingly!
Let me introduce myself: I'm a researcher who has come to assist you. Call me Enjou.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: My main duty is to organize and translate clues regarding the trial to guide you on your path.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's nice. We've always had to rely on our own memory to figure the puzzles we encountered elsewhere.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Wow! You know what? You might actually be more professional than me, then! I mean, I'm just a scholar.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But Tsuyuko said...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Tsuyuko... Right. Her. Didn't she say that there would be some clerical staff on hand to assist the hero?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She did say something like that...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Exactomundo. I mean, it would be quite a stretch to expect you to learn Byakuyakoku's script from scratch.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: And that's where I come in! I'm here to help translate documents and hints. Any questions for me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do you know about that central tower?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: That's the heart of the trial, a building known as Dainichi Mikoshi — which also means "chariot of the sun."

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: I believe that it should be defended by a barrier right now. Its original purpose was to protect the citizens, but at present, we cannot enter unless it is disabled.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Now I can see the questions bubbling up in your face already, so let me just explain how we're going to break this barrier.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: First, you'll need to find something known as the "Golden Bridle." According to related literature, it's a device that is less than an armful in size.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so it's not a rope?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The name is simply derived from one of Byakuyakoku's legends. They say that the sun and the moon were moved by the chariots of the gods.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: And the Golden Bridle was Byakuyakoku's national treasure.

choices.text: Byakuyakoku's...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: That's right, Byakuyakoku. That's the real name of this place. A nether realm without light. Byakuyakoku — the place where sins piled high in the ever-{RUBY#[S]Tokoyo}night, only to be cleansed, revealing their true colors.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: ...But back to the trial. The people of Byakuyakoku were saved by the Great Serpent, and thus re-attained the light of heaven. They all moved above the depths.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Just so you know, that's what my name means. "Above the depths."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hahaha...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Anyway, the people of Watatsumi archived Byakuyakoku's facilities after leaving that place. As for this place, this is one of those very facilities — the library of Byakuyakoku.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: To facilitate future trials, the Golden Bridle was moved closer by. To the back of the library, to be exact.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: So, finding this Golden Bridle is the first part of the trial. Well, that's what the trial guidebook in the library says, anyway.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you get here earlier than us?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Oh, that? You're the heroes. Yours is the rough, narrow road up to the front gate of the trial. As for us support staff... We have our own side routes and back doors.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Anyone of a more plebeian persuasion who manages to sneak in isn't gonna get very far... Without the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep to open the gate, the trial and its contents will not activate.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Plus, it's not as if ordinary people would understand Byakuyakoku's script, anyway. They wouldn't be able to figure the clues out.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Without the Golden Bridle, there is no entering Enkanomiya and probing the secrets of its eternal night.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: If you really don't trust me, you're free to rough me up a bit. But, ah, don't drag me back to the surface afterwards, thanks.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: As you can see, I'm just a scholar with a thirst for knowledge, and with a certain tome that he must find in Byakuyakoku.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he's said this much, and it certainly doesn't look like he's trying to trick us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon thinks we can trust him for a while, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Haha, thanks for the token of faith. Well, off you get then. This Golden Bridle isn't going to find itself!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this what you're looking for?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Ah, yep. That's the one. You're pretty good at this hero business, aren't you?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The book says that the craftsman "Aberaku n{RUBY#[S]Abrax}o Mikoto" was ordered to create the chariot of the sun to finally bring light to the everlasting night.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Before this, the people lived in a constant state of fear, for it was the great hunters in the dark — the Bathysmal Vishaps — who were the original rulers of this land.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Bathysmal Vishaps?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Yes. Pure, primordial elemental creatures, wild spirits who never bent the knee to any god or worldly power.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: I believe that the traditional Sangonomiya tale, "The Clash of the Drakes and the Serpent," also refers to a Bathysmal Vishap as a Dragonheir of the Depths.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: At first, people would light lamps to chase the dark away, but to little effect. But when the Dainichi Mikoshi was created, the White Night chased the darkness of the Ever-Night away. Thus did the people gain a reprieve with which to live their lives.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The Dainichi Mikoshi could even be used to put forth a barrier to protect the people of Byakuyakoku. With this, we should be able to bring the barrier down.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Let me help you activate it. According to what the book says, I need to do this, then this... and then this. Okay! That should do it!

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The Golden Bridle's ready. Commanding the Dainichi Mikoshi to drop the barrier should be peanuts now!

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: But we should probably perform such portentous deeds at the outermost gates of the Dainichi Mikoshi, wouldn't you say?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The main gate should be on the southeastern section of the area it occupies. Just circle the barrier a bit till you find it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Enjou goes into detail about where the meeting place is.\n...Without really caring if you can understand him or not.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Enkanomiya is surrounded by bottomless chasms. If you fall, you could count to a hundred without ever hitting the bottom, so please, please watch your step.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: In any case, if you can't find the place, just circle around the barrier a bit. You'll get there eventually.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: I'm almost done with my own investigations here. I haven't found what I'm looking for, though, so I'll go on ahead to wait for you.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Oh, one other thing — I believe that this picture behind me matches Enkanomiya's topography. I suggest you study it carefully before heading out.

choices.text: ...National treasure?
Two is plenty.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Have you made any progress looking for the Golden Bridle?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: When I first entered the library, there was a handbook sitting in a most conspicuous position, detailing hints concerning the trial in the ancient tongue. The Golden Bridle should be in the back of this library.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: It seems that you've retrieved all the fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Now, please do not be startled by the next thing I'm about to tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: The Bloodbranch Coral needs to be retrieved from the body of special Bathysmal Vishaps, which are right under the Dainichi Mikoshi...

choices.text: What is it with dragons and being buried underground...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The Vishaps locked beneath it have been adjusted specifically such that they can accept fragments of Watatsumi Omikami's Bloodbranch Coral without experiencing any rejection.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: But these adjustments have also made them exceptionally large, and they're most likely not that easy to kill.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Nonetheless, every good trial must end with the hero defeating the wicked dragon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we'll have to find them after all?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Indeed, that is so. As such, you shall have to complete three more Trials of Valor before the way will open for you.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: If you cannot complete these trials, I doubt that you'll be anything but a free meal for those Bathysmal Vishaps.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: But you need not worry, I believe that it'll be easy enough for you. Or you can treat it as a warm-up, whichever suits you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't you say this to everyone who comes this way? You're just an afterimage with some self-awareness, aren't you?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Eh? You don't look like much, but you're actually smarter than our Watatsumi heroes. Interesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nah, you guys just have too little brain juice to go around!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, wait a moment. What Paimon wanted to say is: won't you cause the heroes to underestimate the trial if you talk like this?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: I know. This is the "sin of deception." But the coral's retrieval is something that concerns the survival of Watatsumi.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The heroes are only here because they're determined to see this through. All I can do at this point is push them forward.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: In name, at least, I am a sinless "Shade of Tokoyo" born for ritual purpose. But on this level, I suppose I am not myself free of transgression.

choices.text: (Sorry to disappoint you...)

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Allow me to awaken the last three testing grounds.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Please wait a moment.

choices.text: (But we're actually here for the treasure...)
Quite the surprise...

talks.objective: Examine the mechanism and open the great door

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: The three trial areas have been prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Now, allow me to give you the clues to clearing them.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Now, in this Evernight, gaze upon the borders of Byakuyakoku.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: "In the faintness of everlasting night, beyond the rushing of the river Styx, within the sinless flow of heavenly light."

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, hero, would you mind listening to some of my personal thoughts? Hmm, come to think of it, the fact that I have such thoughts, means that my original self must've had such frustrations as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: The war between us and the Bathysmal Vishaps can be traced back to ancient times. Once upon a time, this was a brutal battle for survival.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: But... Now that we are about to live above the surface, we will no longer fight with them over territory.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: It's just that the threat of Holy Soil that the Vassals of Watatsumi warned us of will never cease. Watatsumi Omikami also warned us that its days shall be numbered once it returns to land.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: We have done a great wrong to the Bathysmal Vishaps. For fear of our future, we did something awful to them.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: "To know sin is to be free of it." Such magical words do not convince me at all, for according to this law, all the people of Watatsumi are bearers of sin.

choices.text: (I'm not sure I get what this is about...)

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: It seems that I've spoken too much.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Well then, let me help you put the Reins of Revival together. You will need it as proof of your worthiness during the trials.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Aru puts the three fragments and the Golden Bridle together...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: From now on, the kingship of Byakuya and Enkanomiya are in your hands.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: This way, you may release the seal on The Emanant Skylight. Then, you may ascend to the Gate of Heaven and access the site of the trial.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Emanant Skylight?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: It's one part of the ritual. All heroes who initiate the trial must obtain the Reins of Revival. Only by proving yourself that way can you proceed to the next step.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: At night, you can see three pillars of light that descend from the dome above. These pillars point unto The Emanant Skylight.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Take the Reins of Revival there, and you will understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're speaking in riddles!

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Sorry. I delivered these lines from memory according to Sangonomiya's script. I mean, aren't unclear instructions also part of the tradition of such trials?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Whatever the case may be. All the Jibashiri at the trial area are weirdos. If you don't pass through the teleporter to get there, they won't speak gently to you.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Either way, I can only stay here and hope that you will conquer all the obstacles set before you, and that you will return crowned in recognition.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Ah, right. Due to the power of the Reins of Revival, Enkanomiya will now show you a different side of itself. You should meet various afterimages along your path.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: But they are not quite the same as this ritual afterimage of mine. These people have been chosen by the undying principles of Enkanomiya due to their powerful emotions, and their transgression has resulted in an afterimage being created.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: They are what the Jibashiri call the Shades of Tokoyo. But bear in mind the principle that "to know sin is to be free of it." Do not tell them that they are afterimages.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The other afterimages are not like me. The moment they realize that they are shadows of their former selves, they will dissipate.

choices.text: We've seen someplace similar in Liyue.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: On the other hand, we people of Enkanomiya have gotten used to it by now. Well then, good luck to you.

choices.text: This place really is quite curious.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: #Check you out, {NICKNAME}! You actually defeated these Bathysmal Vishaps all by yourself! Impressive, most impressive indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Can I touch them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Enjou? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Hah. Actually, I'm gonna touch 'em no matter what you say. These are the mortal foes of humanity, after all. This chance may never come again!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Ah, oh yes, you must be wondering how I got here. Well, bear with me a moment. I need to think about where to start explaining.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Simply put, Enkanomiya is the netherworld of sinners, yes? I am one such sinner — one who has committed the sins of deception and betrayal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait, Paimon still doesn't get it... What are you trying to do, Enjou?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I came here to search for a certain book. That book contains records of things that happened in Byakuyakoku before the Dainichi Mikoshi was constructed.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: These chronicles are known to the people here as the times "before Sun and Moon." Back then, no gods walked the earth, and the whole land belonged to a single civilization.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was there ever really such a time? The bards claim that the times "when gods walked the earth" is the furthest back we go!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Yes, that's precisely it. That's why I wanted to find this book. That way, we, the Abyss Order, would have proof. Proof that the gods and Celestia came from beyond this world.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: The only thing I do know at the moment is that the Great Serpent was sentenced to death by Celestia for accidentally reading this book.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: An entire nation was relocated, the door to the depths was sealed, and that nation was stirred up in an eastern expedition to cover this truth.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Yes, that was the grand ritual of sacrifice required for the people of Watatsumi to once again live like humans.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: But as for this book... I searched for it in the library and the Dainichi Mikoshi, but I could not find it.

choices.text: That's... too much information.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Wait, I said this much, and that's all you have to say?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Not going to grit your teeth in anger, or just dispense with that and smack me in the face?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Do you seriously want to get beaten up that badly?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: But actually, I don't think I did anything THAT bad. I didn't technically lie to you — I am a clerical staff member sent to help you... I just never said that I was sent by Sangonomiya.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: I was indeed translating literature here, but you know, it had nothing to do with the trial. I am a bookish character, and hey — did I or did I not transform into a fire-flinging monster!?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: ...I believe that you refer to our exegetes as "Lectors," yes?

choices.text: So you tricked us, then?

talks.objective: Talk to the person on the second floor

Two is plenty.

talks.objective: Go to the back of the library and seek out the Golden Bridle

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! It's the Abyss Order. Are these the "scurrying rats" that Tsuyuko was referring to?

talks.objective: Investigate the rear of the library and solve the puzzle
Go to the library and talk to Enjou

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Have you made any progress looking for the Golden Bridle?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this what you're looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Ah yes, that's the one! Why, isn't this a coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: But we should probably perform such portentous deeds at the outermost gates of the Dainichi Mikoshi, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: The main gate should be on the southeastern section of the area it occupies. Just circle the barrier a bit till you find it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Enjou goes into detail about where the meeting place is.\n...Without really caring if you can understand him or not.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Enkanomiya is surrounded by bottomless chasms. If you fall, you could count to a hundred without ever hitting the bottom, so please, please watch your step.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: In any case, if you can't find the place, just circle around the barrier a bit. You'll get there eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I'm almost done with my own investigations here. I haven't found what I'm looking for, though, so I'll go on ahead to wait for you.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Byakuyakoku has a tradition of triangle worship.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: They believed that Byakuyakoku was the intersection between three realms: the Vishap Realm, the Human Realm, and the Void Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: The three trial sites on the border were originally watch-posts against the Vishaps, and they were also a spiritual junction for the three powers that flowed through Enkanomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: In that triangular formation of nature, there was an opposition between the abyssal Void Realm and the elemental Vishap Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Humans would create high towers in later years to allow the Human Realm to interpose itself between the two, thus creating a stable space — one held up by three towers in three corners.

talks.objective: Follow Enjou's instructions and explore up ahead
Follow Enjou's instructions and explore up ahead
Follow Enjou's instructions and explore up ahead
Go to the broken bridge in front of the Dainichi Mikoshi

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Allow me to help you shut the barrier down. Could you pass me the Golden Bridle?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I suddenly have some reservations...)

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Huh? Still suspicious of me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Enjou, don't you think you're a bit too quick on your feet?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Oh, come now, that's hurtful talk, though I suppose that the sight of a literary researcher bouncing about the place happily is a rare one.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: But come now, I didn't deceive you earlier, did I?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's true. We couldn't have found the Golden Bridle without your help.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I mean, this will definitely sound like villain-talk, but: Aha, only I can help you now!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: You can hold me at sword-point, or hit me to make up for the time you didn't earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: But once you're done with that, I'd like you to trust me. If you don't, none of us are going to enter the Dainichi Mikoshi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Are you the type who enjoys getting beaten up or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Not that Paimon's going to do that! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: (Hang on, I'm rolling my sleeves up.)

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Err... W—Wait just a moment there. Y—You're joking, right? I've got a glass jaw!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Okay, okay, stop scaring him already. Just give him the Bridle, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Okay then. Now, allow me to help you bring this barrier down. Please step back a bit.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: This is my first time, after all. Things, uh, could go poorly. You never know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What could happen?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: For example, the blast could send you tumbling into a bottomless chasm. Or the fetid air might make it hard to breathe. Or maybe some giant guardian dragon might come charging out...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Or I might even get cursed and turn into some sort of flame-flinging monster.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That's kinda scary.

choices.text: (Hand the Golden Bridle over.)

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Okay then. Now, allow me to help you bring this barrier down. Please step back a bit.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: This is my first time, after all. Things, uh, could go poorly. You never know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What could "go poorly"?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: For example, the blast could send you tumbling into a bottomless chasm. Or the fetid air might make it hard to breathe. Or maybe some giant guardian dragon might come charging out...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Or I might even get cursed and turn into some sort of flame-flinging monster.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... That's kinda scary.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Have you found all the fragments?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: See? I told you! We're the unbeatable trio!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Quick, go give them to Aru. Once you can see all the afterimages in Enkanomiya, you should be able to discover still more secrets.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Ah, I gotta say, opening ancient ruins for the first time in my life feels pretty exciting!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Watching that huge wall disappear really gives you that kind of rush you get from burning a huge library, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That sounds really dangerous. You sure you're a researcher?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Of course! I already can't wait to investigate the insides of the Dainichi Mikoshi. What long-lost volumes will we uncover there?

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Well, allow me to go ahead first. If you find any tempting treasures, you're free to take them.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Have you found all the fragments?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's someone upstairs!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Aaahh!! Ghost! I—It's a ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eeeek!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, Enjou! You scared Paimon more than this ghostly guy over here!

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: *cough* I, uh, sorry. I—I'm fine now. Mostly.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: B—Byakuyakoku, due to its properties as a nether realm... sometimes projects shadows of the past based on remnant thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Though their stories have already ended, who they were at that moment is captured and retained. They can even interact with you.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: Such powerful emotions are called the "Sins of Tokoyo."

choices.text: "Powerful emotions"...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Thus, these unique ley line phenomena are known as "Sinshades" or "Shades of Tokoyo."
...So, my current form will be visible to future heroes as well, then?
That's good to know. Guess I don't have to be nervous after all, huh? The future me is going to act based on current me's memories.
...Still nervous, though.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: What in the world... It's talking!
Ah. Seems like our heroes have arrived. Hello there. My Watatsumi name is Aru, and my original Byakuyakoku name is Argos.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: I'm in charge of explaining the next step of the trial, which is to restore the "Reins of Revival" and display your royal right over this land.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The Reins of Revival are a national treasure that can be used to command the spirits of the nether to speak, and they are made of the same material as the Dainichi Mikoshi.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The Reins must be pieced together with the Golden Bridle as their core. As such, you need to find three other fragments.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Ah, and if you have any other questions, feel free to ask. I believe that my leftover spiritual essence should be able to answer your questions.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you like eating Butter Crab?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Wh—What is that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then do you like some fresh fish sashimi?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Huh, that reminds me. Recently, Watatsumi Omikami has raised land for us above the sea's surface, so we should be able to start shallow sea fishing. The variety of edible fish should also increase.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: ...But yes, back on topic. The three fragments have been hidden in three key locations around the Dainichi Mikoshi. These would be The Narrows, the Evernight Temple, and the Serpent's Heart.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: And when I say "hidden," I do mean hidden. The officials in charge of setting the trial up are very capable indeed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No problem. We've faced loads of tricky puzzles before...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: If you see the altar at the Serpent's Heart, you may want to search that place thoroughly for clues. A Jibashiri spent all day setting them up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jibashiri?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The special officer corps Chthonios, the armed judges of the nether in Byakuyakoku. That's who the "Jibashiri" are.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: They possessed tokens made out of a special material that could cause the souls of Byakuyakoku to reveal themselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... doesn't sound like an Inazuman name at all.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Well, Watatsumi Island was a product of the Archon War. Before that...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Byakuyakoku's histories are filled with names like Abrax, Spartacus, Chthonios, Gigantus, and such.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Hmm. So is this human culture where the divine envoys do not interfere too much...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What did you say?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Ah, er, nothing. Just the bad habit of a bookworm. Keep listening to Argos.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Ah, yes. Now that the Evernight has arrived, all of Enkanomiya will show you a different side of itself. You should meet various afterimages along your path.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: But they are not quite the same as this ritual afterimage of mine. These people have been chosen by the undying principles of Enkanomiya due to their powerful emotions, and their transgression has resulted in an afterimage being created.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: They are what the Jibashiri call the Shades of Tokoyo. But bear in mind the principle that "to know sin is to be free of it." Do not tell them that they are afterimages.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The other afterimages are not like me. The moment they realize that they are shadows of their former selves, they will dissipate.

choices.text: We've seen someplace similar in Liyue.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: On the other hand, we people of Enkanomiya have gotten used to it by now. Well then, good luck to you.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Well, I'll be waiting here for good news from you.

choices.text: This place really is quite curious.
"Sins"...

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can help you with?

choices.text: About the fragment at the Evernight Temple...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The fragment is said to have been hidden in a secret part of the Temple. Its gates will only open at night.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The fragment contains the power of the "Serpent-Seeker Rule," which will attract Vishaps.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: As such, you can follow their trail to find the fragment. But there will be monsters remaining there and standing guard, so it is best to be careful.

choices.text: Tell me about the fragment at the Serpent's Heart...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The Serpent's Heart is home to an altar that is considered the heart of the Cosmic Serpent. Before the coming of Watatsumi Omikami, we called this place The Heart of Ouroboros.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: It is, in essence, a sealing device for storing important objects. Using a phenomenon unique to Enkanomiya known as the Sunfire Phantasms, we added another dimension of possibilities to that device.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: As such, that place was already known as Delphi, the Serpent's Land, even before the coming of Watatsumi Omikami.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The proper entry procedures must be followed in strict order to retrieve the corresponding objects from their locations. As such, this place can also be used to imprison criminals.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The codes have been scattered throughout Enkanomiya. If you find them, some other rewards may yet await.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: One of the fragments is within the altar. As for any secret messages regarding it, they should be found near the altar — it took a real scolding from Lady Eboshi before those were added in, too.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: By the way, when you are out searching for clues, watch out for Enkanomiya's Whitenight and Evernight states.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: There is also a type of ley line phenomenon here known as Sunfire Phantasms. As the land phases between Whitenight and Evernight, energy will gather and disperse. This can cause objects to be hidden or become visible.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: If you cannot find clues but discover certain irregularities, try switching between day and night.

choices.text: As for the fragment at the Narrows...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The ruins of the Narrows contains a hidden chamber. Its exact position is yours to discover alone.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The entrance to the chamber has been concealed by a Sunfire Phantasm. It can only be revealed by switching between Whitenight and Evernight.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: In later days, we would come to grasp the phenomenon known as the Sunfire Phantasms and use them to conceal secrets.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Matters related to the trial are of utmost secrecy, so please, simply rely on your observational skills and the changes between night and day to explore on your own.

choices.text: I've got nothing else to ask...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Understood. If you require help, feel free to seek me out at any time — though I fear that I can only answer specific questions you may have in my current state...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: These afterimages really are interesting...

choices.text: About the movement of the sun and moon here...

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Well, we are underground, so there is no sun here. That is why the people here created this lighthouse.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Through this and perhaps other devices as well, the rulers of Byakuyakoku could adjust a solar and lunar cycle, thus alternating between Whitenight and Evernight.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: In ancient times, the Dainichi Mikoshi's name was "Hyperion," which refers to the main body of the sun in the ancient tongue.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: I can understand their sentiments. Everything must have been hard, living in a realm bereft of the sun.

choices.text: Is there anything else you know about Byakuyakoku?

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Byakuyakoku has a tradition of triangle worship.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: They believed that Byakuyakoku was the intersection between three realms: the Vishap Realm, the Human Realm, and the Void Realm.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: The three trial sites on the border were originally watch-posts against the Vishaps, and they were also a spiritual junction for the three powers that flowed through Enkanomiya.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: In that triangular formation of nature, there was an opposition between the abyssal Void Realm and the elemental Vishap Realm.

response.speaker: Enjou
response.text: Humans would create high towers in later years to allow the Human Realm to interpose itself between the two, thus creating a stable space — one held up by three towers in three corners.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: "Watatsumi is pronounced guilty of the following sins: four counts of the sin of profanity, and a further eight counts for the sin of deceiving living souls."

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: "With this stone I seal the everlasting, that transgressions past shall not be pursued."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you talking about, Aru?

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: This is my final task, which is that I must read this blessing. Its meaning is that Watatsumi Omikami has carried all our transgressions and gone to its death.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: There is one last thing I must ask of you. When you have left Enkanomiya, tell no one of anything regarding the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: This is how all previous trials have been conducted — and I hope you can keep it this way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Next, you must prove your valor against the Bathysmal Vishaps underneath the Mikoshi— *sigh* You know what? This isn't the way I want to put this.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: You are there for the Bloodbranch Corals that were grafted onto their bodies, and they will not simply roll over and let you do it.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: They will unleash upon you the grudge that they have nursed over many long years against humanity.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: This will, without a doubt, be a mortal struggle. Sangonomiya's survival is in your hands. Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: It seems that you've retrieved all the fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: I'm not sure if you've realized this during the course of your adventures...

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: But it is no longer important. Now, please do not be startled by what I'm about to tell you—

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: The Bloodbranch Coral needs to be retrieved from the body of special Bathysmal Vishaps, which are right under the Dainichi Mikoshi...

choices.text: What is it with dragons and being buried underground...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The Vishaps locked beneath it have been adjusted specifically such that they can accept fragments of Watatsumi Omikami's Bloodbranch Coral without experiencing any rejection.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: But these adjustments have also made them exceptionally large, and they're most likely not that easy to kill.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Nonetheless, every good trial must end with the hero defeating the wicked dragon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we'll have to fight after all, huh?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: That is the case. But you need not worry. The Vishap swarm is not your match.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's pretty confident in {NICKNAME}'s skills too. But can you prove what you just said?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Hahaha, not at all. This is simply the default encouragement.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That seems mighty irresponsible of you. Aren't you just giving your heroes blind confidence like that?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Huh. You know, you don't look like much, but you're actually brighter than our Watatsumi heroes. Interesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nah, you guys just have too little brain juice to go around!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, wait, no. Paimon was just saying that this isn't right!

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: I know. This is the "sin of deception." But the coral's retrieval is something that concerns the survival of Watatsumi.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The heroes are only here because they're determined to see this through. All I can do at this point is push them forward.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: I have faith in the people of Watatsumi, and I believe in those that shall come after us.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: In name, at least, I am a sinless "Shade of Tokoyo" born for ritual purpose. But on this level, I suppose I am not myself free of transgression.

choices.text: (Sorry to disappoint you...)

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: In that case, allow me to help you put the Reins of Revival together.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Though I suppose the name "Reins of Revival" is not entirely accurate. It was originally written as the "Reins of Recovery" — namely, the "recovery of control over things that return from beyond the grave."

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: The chariot of the sun brings light in the day, and by night come the spirits of the past. The one who bears the Reins may master both the light and the gloom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Speaking of which, where did Enjou go?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: That person looked up and down the Dainichi Mikoshi for a while before displaying some displeasure and leaving. It seems that he had not found what he was searching for.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: I am quite certain that he is not of any Watatsumi bloodline. He also has some kind of special art on his person that may be able to disrupt the ritual or cause me to dissipate.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: I am one who guides the heroes, and cannot act rashly. If I were to disappear, these trials would also cease. I cannot allow such an outcome.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Thus, while he is not near, I must caution you to be wary of him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we wouldn't have been able to find the Golden Bridle without his help. We might not even have reached the Dainichi Mikoshi at all!

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Is that so? Perhaps I am overthinking things. After all, only the trusted retainers of the Sangonomiya would know the ancient language of Watatsumi. Of course, there is another possibility...

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: But it is likely no large problem. Long years have passed since, and time grinds all civilizations into dust.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: ...But let us return to the trial. I shall open the path to the final trial.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: "Watatsumi is pronounced guilty of the following sins: four counts of the sin of profanity, and a further eight counts for the sin of deceiving living souls."

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: "With this stone I seal the everlasting, that transgressions past shall not be pursued."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you talking about, Aru?

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: This is my final task, which is to read this blessing. Its meaning is that Watatsumi Omikami is about to carry all our transgressions and go to its death.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: There is one last thing I must ask of you. When you have left Enkanomiya, tell no one of anything regarding the trial.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: This is how all previous trials have been conducted — and I hope you can keep it this way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I understand.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: Next, you must prove your valor against the Bathysmal Vishaps underneath the Mikoshi— *sigh* You know what? This isn't the way I want to put this.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: You are there for the Bloodbranch Corals that were grafted onto their bodies, and they will not simply roll over and let you do it.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: They will unleash upon you the grudge that they have nursed over many long years against humanity.

response.speaker: Aru
response.text: This will, without a doubt, be a mortal struggle. Sangonomiya's survival is in your hands. Good luck.

choices.text: (But we're actually here for the treasure...)
Quite the surprise...

talks.objective: Open the way to the final trial
Go to the base of the Dainichi Mikoshi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's with this Enjou guy, and why did he just run off by himself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Enkanomiya might have been emptied, but that's way too reckless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know what? Paimon still thinks he's kinda fishy...

talks.objective: Defeat the Abyss Lector: Fathomless Flames
Talk to the thing calling itself "Enjou"

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: Phew... Wow. I didn't underestimate you, goodness no, but... I suppose a clerk is ultimately no match for a hero.

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: I wanted to get rid of you and then find some disguise with which I could claim that your mission was a failure. I mean, there's got to be some stories in which the hero doesn't slay the dragon. But oh well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why did you attack us?

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: You mean, why wouldn't I, right? I'm a creature writhing in the Abyss, and you're a mortal walking in the sun.

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: You did defeat a lot of my subordinates and comrades on your way here, too. So you can consider this revenge from a sentimental perspective.

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: I mean, I was also thinking... "See, I can't find this book no matter where I look. Might it be with you? Perhaps I should dispose of you and then search you."

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: Also, "Hmm. This person here is carrying all these Mint, Cabbage, and Fowl... I wonder what they're trying to do."

dialogues.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
dialogues.text: ...Well, you get the picture. There are lots of reasons why I should kill you. As for reasons against, there's only one: "I rather like you." Could you think of another?

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
response.text: Ahahah!

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
response.text: Yes, yes, I failed. And we all learned a little something today, didn't we? I suppose you shouldn't trust people that easily in the future, eh?

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
response.text: Take that little fellow by your side. Perhaps you shall someday face betrayal from that corner too. Who knows?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, hey! You trying to split us up here?

choices.text: Paimon wouldn't turn on me.

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
response.text: Oh, come on. You didn't learn anything at all!

response.speaker: The Thing Calling Itself "Enjou"
response.text: ...Well, whatever. We haven't much time left to talk. I'll depart for now. We'll meet again.

choices.text: Paimon doesn't really have much capacity for betrayal.
How about "not taking on someone you can't beat"?

talks.objective: Return to Sangonomiya Shrine and talk to Tsuyuko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tsuyuko, we found the Bloodbranch Coral.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Ah, our great hero, our gallant warrior, our mighty paragon, our destined savior! On behalf of Madam Kokomi and all the people of Watatsumi Island, I give you my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: You look exhausted. Perhaps it was too taxing a task to send you down alone after all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not alone! Paimon was there too! ...And then there was this other guy who sneaked in. He did help us a lot at first...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #But in the end... Ugh, this is a long story. It's the main reason why {NICKNAME}'s so exhausted, too.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: It seems like something that Madam Kokomi did not anticipate occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Did one who seemed like a mere thief with a Watatsumi language dictionary turn out to be something far more troublesome?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was someone from the Abyss Order.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: ...This... This is very grave news. I will report it to Madam Kokomi.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: However, since you have returned with the branch, it will soon come time for her to see to the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: I will go and pull her out of her room now.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: #Whatever the case, {NICKNAME}, please accept our gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: It seems that you have completed all the trials and thus displayed your valor. Now then. Display the Reins of Revival, and display your kingship over Byakuyakoku.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Though I suppose the name "Reins of Revival" is not entirely accurate. It was originally written as the "Reins of Recovery" — namely, the "recovery of control over things that return from beyond the grave."

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: The chariot of the sun brings light in the day, and by night come the spirits of the past. The one who bears the Reins may master both the light and the gloom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Speaking of which, where did Enjou go?

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: That person looked up and down the Dainichi Mikoshi for a while before displaying some displeasure and leaving. It seems that he had not found what he was searching for.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: I am quite certain that he is not of any Watatsumi bloodline. He also has some kind of special art on his person that may be able to disrupt the ritual or cause me to dissipate.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: I am one who guides the heroes, and cannot act rashly. If I were to disappear, these trials would also cease. I cannot allow such an outcome.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Thus, while he is not near, I must caution you to be wary of him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we wouldn't have been able to find the Golden Bridle without his help. We might not even have reached the Dainichi Mikoshi at all!

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Is that so? Perhaps I am overthinking things. After all, only the trusted retainers of the Sangonomiya would know the ancient language of Watatsumi. Of course, there is another possibility...

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: But it is likely no large problem. Long years have passed since, and time grinds all civilizations into dust.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Regardless, let us return to the trial. I shall open the path to the final trial.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: "Watatsumi is pronounced guilty of the following sins: four counts of the sin of profanity, and a further eight counts for the sin of deceiving living souls."

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: "With this stone I seal the everlasting, that transgressions past shall not be pursued."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you talking about, Aru?

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: This is my final task, which is to read this blessing. Its meaning is that Watatsumi Omikami is about to carry all our transgressions and go to its death.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: There is one last thing I must ask of you. When you have left Enkanomiya, tell no one of anything regarding the trial.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: This is how all previous trials have been conducted — and I hope you can keep it this way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: Next, you must prove your valor against the Bathysmal Vishaps underneath the Mikoshi— *sigh* You know what? This isn't the way I want to put this.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: You are there for the Bloodbranch Corals that were grafted onto their bodies, and they will not simply roll over and let you do it.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: They will unleash upon you the grudge that they have nursed over many long years against humanity.

dialogues.speaker: Aru
dialogues.text: This will, without a doubt, be a mortal struggle. Sangonomiya's survival is in your hands. Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I was waiting for you two.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: You now control the hub of Enkanomiya... No, Byakuyakoku. Here, try touching this device.

dialogues.speaker: Enjou
dialogues.text: I wager it'll be quite the experience.

dialogues.speaker: Eboshi
dialogues.text: Congratulations, hero of Sangonomiya. You have obtained the blood-branch of coral.

dialogues.speaker: Eboshi
dialogues.text: My name is Erebos. In the Inazuman tongue, that would be Eboshi.

dialogues.speaker: Eboshi
dialogues.text: You have proven here that your valor is beyond compare — that you are a worthy savior of Sangonomiya's people. Thus, you have earned the right to ask and to be answered.

dialogues.speaker: Eboshi
dialogues.text: Still, I ask that you follow the rules and not take the truth beyond this ocean abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Eboshi
dialogues.text: What else do you wish to know?

choices.text: Tell me about the Bathysmal Vishaps...

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: They are primordial elemental beings, unbent and unbowed by the power that came from the heavens owing to their living deep underwater.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: They are actually very intelligent, and they are adept at evolving. They would even evolve into different elemental forms throughout the history of their war against us.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: I would not be surprised at all if they have learned language or perhaps even evolved into lizard-people of a sort.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: The Holy Soil phenomenon is, in fact, the expansion of their habitat. That means that the primordial elemental power of the three realms is growing stronger.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Only by using Watatsumi Omikami's life force to awaken its second servant could we convert this raw, raging elemental power.

choices.text: Tell me about Watatsumi Omikami...

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Watatsumi Omikami, due to ill-fortune, fell into this place, beyond the jurisdiction of the heavenly order.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: But this was undoubtedly to the good fortune of us, the people of Byakuyakoku. It has done a great many things for us.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Unfortunately, by making contact with us, it also grasped a truth that came before its own existence. Thus, it was forced to seek a valiant death.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Thus, the people would no longer suspect that there might be secrets that lay hidden in the shadows. This was the only way the people of Byakuyakoku would be allowed to live under the rule of The Seven.

choices.text: So, what were things like before the sun and moon?

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Before Byakuyakoku fell into the deep sea, the whole world had a single unified culture.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Later, a great war broke out, in which the heavens capsized and the earth was ripped asunder. This land was then plunged into the dark ocean depths.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: However, the heavenly order seemed to not wish for those who remembered all this to remain on the earth. We searched and searched for a road of return, but there was none to be found.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Much, much later, heaven's powers of prohibition would gradually weaken. Thus did Watatsumi Omikami manage to fall into this place.

choices.text: Tell me about the Dainichi Mikoshi.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: The Dainichi Mikoshi was constructed by the Sage Abrax. It has the power to bring light to the dark depths.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: It has quite a few other functions, to boot.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: All in all, it is a very powerful device.

choices.text: I've got nothing else to ask.

response.speaker: Eboshi
response.text: Fair enough. Again, please remember to keep all that you have seen here in Enkanomiya an eternal secret.
